title: The First Aorist Indicative (Active and Middle)

words.m: ἀπό (from, L6) + λύω (I loose, L2) — to *loose* someone *from* a place or duty = *release, dismiss*

words.m: sounds like "day" — "it's deadline *day*: it *must* be done!"; always followed by an infinitive (L2) saying what is necessary
from δίκαιος (righteous, L5) + the noun ending -σύνη (the *state* of being): the *quality* of being righteous = *righteousness*
ἐκεῖνος (that, L8) — "ek-" out *there*; both start with ἐκεῖ-: "that one, over *there*"
ἐπί (on, toward, L11) + στρέφω (to turn): "strophe" — the *turn* in a Greek chorus/poem; turning *toward* a place = *return*; twin of ὑποστρέφω (L13)

words.m: sounds like "AY-day" — "it's *already* A-day!" — the time has come before you expected
"idiosyncrasy" — a habit that is *one's own*; "idiom" — a phrase *owned* by one language
sounds like "him-AH-tee-on" — "*him*, at tea, *on* in his *garment*"; the cloak you have *on*
"cephalic" — relating to the *head*; "encephalitis" — inflammation inside the *head*; "hydrocephalus" (water on the head)
sounds like "crazy" — a *crazy* person *cries out* in the street

vf.e: I was crying out / they were crying out

a: you all used to cry out
you all used to call out

words.m: "holocaust" (whole + burnt) and "holistic" — the *whole* picture; in predicate position it means "all of / the whole of" (L5 adjective positions)
sounds like "pay-tho" — "I'll *pay*, though" is how you *persuade* someone; same root as πιστεύω (I believe, L2) and πιστός (faithful, L5): being *persuaded* → trust

words.m: ὑπό (under, L9) + στρέφω (to turn): "strophe" — a *turn*; *turn* back *under* = *return*; same meaning as ἐπιστρέφω (L13)

vf.e: I was returning / they were returning
